jobs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original painted tactical battle sprite sheet. The reference is the fixed character AND compact weapon identity: Kitehook Runner woman brown ponytail, teal headband, cream sleeves, fitted brown leather armor, steel left shoulder/knee guards, teal-and-gold tabard/cape, brown boots with yellow ties, belt rope coil. One COMPACT double-hook staff, not a pike: straight wooden shaft is about 60 percent of her standing height from butt to hook socket; two curved steel hooks at screen RIGHT, teal/gold streamers below hooks, one short slack rope loop on LEFT butt. Preserve that fixed length in every pose; do not extend the shaft to reach the opponent. Right hand is rear/left-screen grip and left hand forward/right-screen grip. Whole body/equipment, consistent camera slightly above three-quarter facing RIGHT and identical anatomical scale, painterly style and palette. Opaque perfectly flat vivid magenta RGB255,0,255 backdrop with no spill, no shadows/floor/text/grid/panels. Broad empty gutters and generous outer margins; entire boots, ponytail, compact hook and rope remain within each cell. No gore or extra equipment. Four equal cells TWO columns TWO rows. TOP LEFT: anticipation, torso drawn back, elbows bent, compact staff horizontal against chest, both hands together near the middle of the short shaft. TOP RIGHT: committed short forward thrust, right foot forward knee bent, left leg braces, torso leans right, both hands extend the SAME short staff toward RIGHT; do not lengthen it. BOTTOM LEFT: recover after thrust, body rises, elbows pull same weapon back to waist. BOTTOM RIGHT: defensive-ready, knees softly bent, compact staff held horizontally across chest with same two hand positions. Preserve reference head/body proportions and equipment. Each complete figure should have same implied standing height. Make actions distinct without changing weapon scale.
